criteria.evidence: Explicit classical width_args, pre-effect validation and literal substitution preserve ISA §§3.1–3.3. Memory shapes are supplied rather than inferred from register width.
criteria.change: Optional clarification in §3.2: “An invocation retains its resolved width_args throughout execution, suspension and reversal.”

criteria.evidence: The revision enumerates permitted symbolic positions and preserves ordinary opcode checks after substitution. ISA §§4.2, 4.6 and 16.2 support the stated width and empty-address distinctions.
criteria.change: Optional clarification in §5.1: “Shape substitution introduces no reference-interpreter instruction and consumes no oracle budget step.”

criteria.evidence: The resolved denotation explicitly retains full-domain, control, adjoint, prefix-reversal and restoration obligations. The xor_width success and B=0 outcomes agree with §5.2; both memory-packing results are correct.
criteria.change: Conformance vectors: add the explicit boundary result “At n=1, B=0 and true control, (x,t,f)=(1,1,1) becomes (1,1,0); false control leaves (1,1,1) unchanged.” This illustrates XOR fault accumulation.

criteria.evidence: Scheduling and estimation receive complete shapes without register ids; cache bindings distinguish instances. The stated 219-recipe ref@0.9 hash was reproduced. The new expansion default should also appear at the existing default’s authoritative location.
criteria.change: Amend §17 item 7: “For an ISA 0.10 object, omission of expansion binds ref version 0.9 with hash 5de4e4995350313e50217880ba1b95de39cd043283b726337d4894efb005d197, for family and non-family regions alike.”

criteria.evidence: Instance-keyed records now resolve the §9.4/§12.3 conflict. Subjects, expected programs, inverse pairs, composition and captured contexts distinguish instances. Version-envelope changes and consumer migration are disclosed; canonical interchange fixtures remain publication work.
criteria.change: In §9.1 state the compatibility default explicitly: “A signature without width_params has no shape parameters; its launch width_args is [], and its certificate region record remains keyed by closure_hash.”

criteria.evidence: The executable script passes all 4,352 tuples and both instance-hash vectors. Its stated limitation is accurate: it checks mathematical witnesses, not parsing, expansion or certificate checking. Universal obligations have explicit hypotheses and a concrete-claim default.
criteria.change: Add to §15: “A composed fixture invokes the same family at widths 1 and 3, requires separate records with slot widths [1,1,4] and [3,3,4], and rejects an attempt to discharge the width-3 obligation using only the width-1 claim.”

criteria.evidence: ISA §3.3 and dialect §8.4, D34 and G-17 support the efficiency/interface classification. Existing literal widths remain available. The mixed-fat-object paragraph explicitly preserves native main, argv/envp, unmarked libc, selected VM closures and corresponding native comparison.
criteria.change: Optional standing-check fixture in §15: “Launching a marked family from a native executable requires certificates for its selected VM closure and reached instances, without requiring certificates for unrelated native functions.”

criteria.evidence: The revised rules decide the previously missing semantics and provide actionable consumer obligations. The remaining work is consolidating those rules into canonical grammar and interchange examples before adoption.
criteria.change: In §16.2 state: “A family header appends [p0, p1, …] immediately after its symbol; every family call appends [s0, s1, …] in the same parameter order.” Publish a canonical xor_width[n] object with width_params=[{name:"n",bind:{group:"in",slot:0}}] and its two-instance certificate fixture.

previous_status.note: Explicit call and launch width_args supply A/W; mathematical width checks precede effects, and coherent calls preserve both axes.
Concrete family records are instance-keyed, with resolved signatures, frames, claims and composition references.
The unavailable caller descriptor is no longer presumed; equal-total-width memory shapes remain explicitly distinct.
Separate instance records and preserved argument/body/template shape contexts support both widths within one composed certificate.

suggestions: Identity, expansion and schedules / §17 item 7: repeat the explicit override at the existing default rule: “ISA 0.10 uses the published ref@0.9 catalog by default, including for non-family regions.” The expected catalog hash remains 5de4e4995350313e50217880ba1b95de39cd043283b726337d4894efb005d197. This is consolidation of the proposed default, not a request for a new catalog.

Conformance vectors / §§15–16.2: publish a canonical family object and a bound mixed-width certificate alongside the mathematical script. State: “The checker recomputes each instance hash, substitutes its signature, and validates that record’s frame and claims independently.” Expected child slot widths are [1,1,4] and [3,3,4]; replacing either instance hash with the other must reject before replay.

Release / §9.1: state the non-family default explicitly: “Absent width_params means an empty parameter list; non-family launch requests carry width_args=[], and existing non-family certificate keys remain closure hashes.” This makes migration straightforward without altering the proposal’s semantics.
path_to_accept: Already acceptable as the proposed 0.10 extension. To raise C8 from 4 to 5, publish the canonical grammar productions and one complete family/two-instance certificate fixture. Retain the explicit version boundary; this acceptance does not endorse silently changing published 0.9 identities.
summary: LPE-1, LPE-2, B1 and B2 are resolved. No new S0 issue or false technical premise was found. The mathematical witnesses and catalog hash pass verification, and the mixed-fat-object standing check is satisfied. Accept the proposed 0.10 extension.
